unsupported_codes.reason: Acute maxillary sinusitis: names a sinus that the provider's diagnosis does not name; the tenderness over the cheeks is an exam finding.
Acute frontal sinusitis: names a sinus that the provider's diagnosis does not name.
Acute ethmoidal sinusitis: names a sinus that the provider's diagnosis does not name.
Acute sphenoidal sinusitis: names a sinus that the provider's diagnosis does not name.
Acute pansinusitis: states that all sinuses are involved, which the provider's diagnosis does not say.
Other acute sinusitis: assumes a statement about which sinuses are involved, and the provider's diagnosis makes none.

citations.J01.90: ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY2027, Section I.B.18: when sufficient clinical information is not known or available to assign a more specific code, it is acceptable to report the appropriate unspecified code, and it would be inappropriate to select a specific code that is not supported by the medical record documentation. Section I.A.19: the assignment of a diagnosis code is based on the provider's diagnostic statement that the condition exists. Here the provider's diagnosis is acute sinusitis and names no sinus, so the code for acute sinusitis, unspecified, is reported.

coder_notes: Tenderness over both cheeks is an exam finding, not a diagnosis of maxillary sinusitis. The note records a first episode, so the sinusitis is not recurrent, and ten days of symptoms with a diagnosis of acute sinusitis, so it is not chronic. No organism is identified, so no code from B95-B97 is added. The antibiotic is a seven-day course, so there is no long-term drug therapy code. Congestion, discharge and facial pressure are part of the sinusitis.
